about: Every metric the Developer API dashboard (monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dgx-developer-api.json) and monitoring/prometheus/rules/developer-api.yml query, with its status on 2026-09-13; since 2026-09-29 also every metric monitoring/prometheus/rules/voice-stream.yml (live dictation) reads. check_metrics.py proves the dashboard and developer-api.yml against a running Prometheus; tests/test_developer_api_monitoring.py proves every queried name, voice-stream.yml's included, is listed here. Histograms are listed by base name; their _bucket/_sum/_count series belong to the entry.

statuses.live: Has series in production Prometheus now.
statuses.event_driven: Emitted by merged code, but the series only exists after the first event (a counter or histogram registered on first use). Absent is normal.
statuses.pending: Emitted by code that is written but not merged or not deployed. Absent until it is; panels are titled [pending].
statuses.proposed: Nothing emits it. The README's metric contract says what to emit, where, and with which closed label values. Panels are titled [proposed].

vllm:num_requests_running.source: vLLM engines, jobs vllm-main and vllm-aux (label service)

vllm:prompt_tokens_total.source: vLLM engines; counted when a prefill ENDS

vllm:iteration_tokens_total.source: vLLM engines; _count is scheduler iterations, also counted at prefill end

http_requests_total.source: vLLM engines' HTTP instrumentation (labels handler, method, status as a class 2xx/4xx/5xx)

llm_admission_lane_active.source: orchestrator/app/admission.py Lane._publish (label lane); set only when a lane is used, so absent after an orchestrator start until the first generation. Hourly samples: present 2026-09-12 11:43Z, 18:43Z-09-13 02:43Z, 07:43Z-08:43Z; absent in between with the orchestrator up.

llm_admission_waiting.source: orchestrator/app/admission.py Lane._publish (label lane); same lazy publication as llm_admission_lane_active. Never above 0 in the hours it existed.

techsara_vllm_state.source: engine controller one-hot (label state); read by the state_now annotation

upload_sessions_open.source: orchestrator/app/health._publish_work_gauges on every /health call (label state: uploading, finalizing). The chat app's chunked upload rail, not the public /v1 Files API (design only on 2026-09-13).

asr_queue_depth.source: orchestrator/app/asr.py _Pool.__aenter__; created on the first transcription. Present 2026-09-04 to 09-11 18:41Z, none since.
asr_queue_depth.defect: POOL (dictation) and BATCH_POOL (video) both publish this unlabelled gauge, last writer wins: reproduced 2026-09-13 with the module, one dictation in flight and a video clip that entered and left BATCH_POOL left asr_active_requests at 0. Fix in asr.py: a `pool` label (dictation, video) declared in metrics.py.

asr_requests_total.source: orchestrator/app/asr.transcribe, dictation only (label result: ok, fail). Public /v1/audio/transcriptions does not pass through it (publicapi/sidecars.py sends its own request).

asr_batch_requests_total.source: orchestrator/app/asr.transcribe_segments, video analysis clips (label result: ok, fail)

asr_request_duration_seconds.source: orchestrator/app/asr.transcribe, successful dictation only, orchestrator wall clock

upload_session_total.source: orchestrator/app/uploads._count_session (labels purpose: dataset, document, video; result: complete, rejected, cancelled, expired)

public_api_engine_in_flight.defect: orchestrator/app/metrics.py bounds the label name `engine` to {main} globally, so every gate is exported as engine="other" and the last gate published overwrites the rest. Fix: _ALLOWED_BY_METRIC entries for this metric and public_api_engine_waiting listing the six gate names.

public_api_engine_waiting.note: Without a mode label a background job waiting up to PUBLIC_API_BACKGROUND_GATE_WAIT_S (3,600 s) by design looks the same as a sync caller about to be refused; PublicApiGateWaitSustained leaves main.long out for that reason.

techsara_host_guard_table_present.source: monitoring/exporters/host-guard/host_guard_textfile.sh, once root installs it and node-exporter runs with --collector.textfile.directory

voice_stream_sessions_active.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py, the live dictation gateway (written on a branch, not deployed on 2026-09-29): streams open in the process, published by a scrape-time collector; no labels

voice_stream_audio_received_seconds_tota.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: seconds of 16 kHz PCM received from browsers, added every few seconds per stream; audio replayed after a reconnect counts again; no labels

voice_stream_sessions_total.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: admitted streams by how they ended, settled exactly once per stream; every value registered at 0

voice_stream_rejections_total.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: streams refused at the handshake or later; capacity covers the gateway's VOICE_LIVE_MAX_STREAMS and an engine that answered capacity

voice_stream_errors_total.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: failures on the server's side, one per failed engine attempt or rejected engine event, so NOT a per-stream count

voice_stream_first_partial_seconds.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: arrival of an utterance's first sample at the gateway to its first partial written to the browser

voice_stream_final_seconds.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: arrival of an utterance's last sample to its final written

voice_stream_event_lag_seconds.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: arrival of the newest sample an event covers to that event written

voice_stream_client_e2e_seconds.source: orchestrator/app/voice_live.py: capture to render as the browser measured it (client_stats every 5 s; untrusted, clamped to 60 s)

stt_stream_active_streams.source: compose/stt-stream/server.py, the live dictation engine on the worker (job stt-stream; written on a branch, not deployed on 2026-09-29): streams admitted and open, per profile

stt_stream_audio_seconds_total.source: compose/stt-stream/server.py: seconds of audio received per profile; the real-time factor's denominator

stt_stream_compute_seconds_total.source: compose/stt-stream/server.py: decode seconds charged per profile, every decode_streams call adding its wall time once for EACH stream in its batch (compute += elapsed x batch size; build spec section 11). Real-time factor = compute / audio, a decode step's wall time over the chunk it decodes: it reaches 1.0 when a decode worker can no longer keep up, and a saturated engine reads exactly 1.0 however far behind it falls; VoiceStreamEngineFallingBehind warns above 0.8. The decode-step histogram observes each call's wall time once

stt_stream_decode_step_seconds.source: compose/stt-stream/server.py: wall time of one decode_streams call per profile; the budget is one chunk (160 ms or 560 ms)

stt_stream_rejections_total.source: compose/stt-stream/server.py: connections refused before a stream was admitted; any other reason is counted as other (build spec section 11). The rules rely on capacity only
